lesson.title: Base and height

lead.text: Pick any side of the triangle as its base. The height is the straight distance from the opposite corner to the line of the base, meeting it at a right angle.
The height is not a sloping side. It is the shortest way across.

steps.headline: The height of a triangle is measured at a right angle to its base.

lead.text: This triangle has base 8 cm and height 5 cm. Picture the rectangle with the same base and height. The triangle covers half of it.

reveal.text: You halved base × height. That is the rule for every triangle.

lead.text: Slide the top corner along a line parallel to the base. The sloping sides change length.

reveal.text: Only the base and the height matter to the area. Neither changed.

steps.headline: A triangle has base 9 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. Find its area.

workedSteps.text: Use the base and the perpendicular height, not a sloping side.
Halve it: a triangle is half the rectangle.

steps.headline: A parallelogram has base 8 cm and height 5 cm. Find its area.

workedSteps.text: A diagonal cuts it into two equal triangles.
Two triangles together make the parallelogram.

lead.text: Choose the base and the height. Check the height meets the base at a right angle.

reveal.text: Base × height, halved. The same steps as the 9 by 4 triangle.

lead.text: You know the area and the base this time, not the height. Base × height ÷ 2 gives the area.

lesson.orientation: Measure perpendicular height and connect triangle area to a parallelogram.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: A rectangular card is 6 cm by 4 cm. It is cut along a diagonal into two identical triangles.

intro.promise: By the end you'll find a triangle's area from its base and perpendicular height, and use the same idea for a parallelogram.

recap.keyIdea: A triangle's area is half of base × perpendicular height, and a parallelogram's is base × perpendicular height.

blocks.text: You found that half of a 6 by 4 card is 12 cm².
You showed that sliding a triangle's top corner leaves its area alone, and that a 30 m² flag with a 10 m base stands 6 m tall.

recap.nextHook: Some shapes are built from several parts. Next, split a shape into pieces you can measure.

questions.prompt: A triangle has base 8 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm. Find its area in square centimetres.
hints: Picture the rectangle with the same base and height.
A triangle covers half that rectangle.
Work out 8 × 5, then halve it.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Half the enclosing rectangle gives 8 × 5 / 2 = 20 cm².

questions.onCorrect: 20 cm². A triangle is half the rectangle with the same base and height: 8 × 5 ÷ 2.

misconceptions.feedback: 40 is the whole 8 by 5 rectangle. A triangle covers half of it.
That adds 8 + 5. Multiply the base by the height, then halve.

questions.prompt: The top corner slides sideways but stays 5 cm above the 8 cm base. What happens to the triangle's area?
hints: Identify which dimensions enter the area formula.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: The base and perpendicular height remain fixed, so base × height / 2 remains unchanged.

choices.label: It increases with the sloping side

questions.onCorrect: The area stays the same. Sliding the top corner keeps the base and the height unchanged.

misconceptions.feedback: The sloping sides change length, but the area uses the height. Does the height change?
The triangle is still there, with the same base and the same height.

questions.prompt: A parallelogram has base 8 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm. Find its area in square centimetres.
hints: A diagonal cuts the parallelogram into two triangles.
Each triangle has area base × height ÷ 2. How many are there?
Two halves make a whole: base × height.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Two equal-area triangles together cover 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

questions.onCorrect: 40 cm². A parallelogram is two equal triangles, so halving cancels: base × height.

misconceptions.feedback: That's one triangle. The parallelogram is made of two.
That adds the base and height. Area multiplies them.

questions.prompt: Find the area of a triangle with base 7 m and perpendicular height 6 m, in square metres.
hints: Use the base and the perpendicular height.
Take half their product.
Calculate 7 × 6 / 2.
questions.onCorrect: 21 m². Halve base × perpendicular height, wherever the top corner sits.

misconceptions.feedback: 42 is the whole 7 by 6 rectangle. A triangle is half of it.
That adds 7 + 6. Multiply, then halve.

questions.prompt: A triangle has area 42 cm² and base 12 cm. Find its perpendicular height in centimetres.
hints: Reverse the triangle area formula.
Double the area before dividing by the base.
Calculate 2 × 42 / 12.
questions.onCorrect: 7 cm. Double the area, then divide by the base.

misconceptions.feedback: That divides 42 by 12 only. Base × height is twice the area, so double first.
That multiplies 42 by 12. Undo the multiplying with division.

questions.prompt: Which distance is the height used with a chosen triangle base?
hints: Look for the right-angle relationship to the base.

acceptedIdeas: The perpendicular distance from the opposite vertex to the base line
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: The height must meet the line containing the chosen base at a right angle.

choices.label: The perpendicular distance from the opposite vertex to the base line

questions.onCorrect: Height is the perpendicular distance from the opposite corner to the base's line.

misconceptions.feedback: A sloping side leans away from the base. The height meets the base at a right angle.
A perimeter is a distance round the edge, and has nothing to do with height.

questions.prompt: What is the area of one triangle, in square centimetres?
hints: What is the area of the whole card?
The cut makes two identical triangles.
Share the card's area between them.
questions.onCorrect: 12 cm². Two identical triangles share the card, so each is half of the rectangle.

misconceptions.feedback: 24 is the whole card. The cut makes two triangles.
That adds 6 + 4. Find the area of the card first.

questions.prompt: Why isn't the sloping side used as the height?
hints: Where does the height meet the base?

acceptedIdeas: The height must meet the base at a right angle, and a sloping side leans.
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: The height must meet the base at a right angle, and a sloping side leans.

choices.label: The height must meet the base at a right angle, and a sloping side leans.
A sloping side is always too long.
Only the base can be used in the area.

questions.onCorrect: Height is measured at a right angle to the base. A sloping side leans away, so it is longer.

misconceptions.feedback: It is longer, but that is the effect. The rule is about the right angle to the base.
The area uses both the base and the height.

questions.prompt: A triangular flag has area 30 m² and a base of 10 m. How tall is it, in metres?
hints: Base × height ÷ 2 gives the area. What is base × height?
Base × height is double the area.
Divide that double by the base.
questions.onCorrect: 6 m. Base × height is twice the area, so divide twice the area by the base.

misconceptions.feedback: 30 ÷ 10 forgets the halving. Base × height is twice the area.
That multiplies area by base. Undo the multiplying with division.

questions.prompt: A parallelogram has base 9 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. Find its area in square centimetres.
hints: A parallelogram is two equal triangles.
Each triangle is base × height ÷ 2.
Two of them give base × height.
questions.onCorrect: 54 cm². A parallelogram's area is base × perpendicular height, with no halving.

misconceptions.feedback: 27 halves it. A parallelogram is two triangles, so don't halve.
That adds 9 + 6. Multiply base by height.

questions.prompt: A triangle has base 10 cm and a sloping side of 13 cm. Its perpendicular height is 12 cm. Which length is the height?
hints: Which length meets the base at a right angle?
questions.onCorrect: 12 cm. The height is the perpendicular distance to the base, not a sloping side.

misconceptions.feedback: 13 cm is a sloping side. The height meets the base at a right angle.
10 cm is the base itself. The height is how far the opposite corner is above it.
